I have been farming these 50 mu for 25 years now. My old man gave me the land when I got married at 22, and over the years I rented more plots from neighbors who went to work in Handan or Beijing. It is me, my wife, and our son at home. The son helps on weekends but works in a factory during the week, so I hire workers for the busy seasons.

Last year I planted 30 mu of stevia and 20 mu of cotton, and I will do the same this year. I learned stevia from my cousin in Dongfu village about ten years ago. He was making good money, so I tried 5 mu first, watched it carefully, then expanded. The price is steady at 6 to 6.5 yuan per jin, much better than cotton at 2.8 yuan. But stevia is picky — it needs more water and fertilizer, and transplanting 8,000 seedlings per mu takes a lot of hired hands. Cotton needs less labor except for spraying, but you have to spray it every 5 to 7 days in July and August or the bollworms will eat everything.

For stevia, I will rotary till the land in late March. Basal fertilizer is one bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu — that is 50 kg, 100 jin. The dealer told me this gives 7.5 kg of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium each. I do not fully remember those numbers, but I know one bag per mu is what works because that is what my cousin uses and his stevia grows the best in the village. Then I topdress twice with another 100 jin of compound total per mu. I also spread 100 jin of chicken manure per mu as basal — my neighbor started doing this and his stevia leaves are darker and thicker. I irrigate 5 times: right after transplanting in mid-April, and then every 15 to 20 days when the weather turns dry. I spray pesticide 8 times — mainly for aphids and leaf spot disease. I use the chengguang variety, it is an improved type, not the old wild kind. Last year I got 500 jin per mu, and I expect the same this year if we do not get a big flood.

For cotton, I use guoxinmian seed, improved variety, about 3 jin per mu. I rotary till and put down one bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu as basal. Then when the plants start flowering in July, I topdress with 50 jin of urea per mu — that is half a bag, about 23 kg, which gives another 11.5 kg of nitrogen. I do not add more phosphorus or potassium later; the basal dose is enough for cotton. I irrigate 3 times: at flowering, at boll setting, and at peak boll period in August. I spray 12 times total — insecticide every week in the hot months, plus herbicide once at the beginning and maybe a growth regulator if the plants grow too tall. Last year I got 550 jin per mu, and I expect about the same.

People ask why I do not switch all 50 mu to stevia. I thought about it, but stevia needs too much transplanting labor. At 30 mu, I already hire 15 workers for two weeks just to get the seedlings in the ground. If I did all 50 mu, I could not find enough people in the village. Also, cotton spreads the risk. If stevia price drops, I still have cotton income to cover the fertilizer bill.

I worry about costs every year. A bag of compound is now 130 yuan, urea is about 60 yuan for 50 jin. For 50 mu, I spend over 10,000 yuan on chemical fertilizer alone, not counting manure or hired labor. But I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad harvest means I cannot pay the rent or the workers; wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved. I watch what the big farms around me do. Old Zhang has 80 mu of stevia and he uses the same rates as me, so I know I am not wrong.
